sandbox_argv:
This exploration produces ONE mechanism. You are one of three independent reviewers; you see the same frozen evidence bundle and the same proposals as the others, and you do not coordinate with them before handing in.
THE RESEARCH OBJECTIVE:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.
THE SCOPE CONTRACT (a proposal that misses it is sent back, not scored):
A proposal is IN SCOPE only when all of this holds:
  1. BEHAVIOUR: it names one training-only behaviour signal (directed item transitions, user-interest branching, sequential co-consumption, popularity-adjusted graph neighbours, behaviour-conditioned assignment weights, ...) and says how it is computed.
  2. HYPERBOLIC GEOMETRY: it names an explicit curved operation (trainable or fixed negative curvature, Poincare or Lorentz distance, exp/log maps, geodesic scoring, curved residual, curved quantization, curved regularization) and where in training or quantization it acts.
  3. REAL COUPLING: one connected computational pathway uses both, so that removing either changes the core computation. A behaviour suffix on an unchanged Euclidean quantizer, a standalone hyperbolic loss beside an unrelated behaviour loss, a geometry name without geometric computation, or inherited unused hyperbolic code do NOT qualify.
  4. TESTABLE EFFECT: it states what should observably change (SID assignment, gradient or parameter update, prefix behaviour predictability, or Stage3 Recall) and names the behaviour-off, geometry-off/Euclidean and both-on comparisons. The three switches must be part of the mechanism, so that the coupling can be shown to be real, but the round RUNS no ablation arm: each candidate is trained once.
  5. MINIMAL SPECIFICATION: equations or pseudocode, inputs and outputs, numerical safeguards and the training cost. No proof and no paper section are required.
SID quality (ER, prefix counts, collisions) is NOT a scope criterion and NOT an admission rule.

EXPERIMENT POLICY (binding on every proposal, implementation and review):
  - ONE candidate, ONE training run, on the frozen budget (3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, the frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping).
  - NO ablation experiments: the behaviour-off, geometry-off and both-on switches must EXIST in the code and must be correct, but no arm is trained with them switched off.
  - NO tuning experiments: no sweep over the coupling weight, the clip bound, the temperature, the usage weight or any other constant. A constant that enters the mechanism has to be DERIVED (a scale-relative bound, a measured quantity, a documented default), not chosen by trying values.
  - NO multi-seed experiments: a candidate is not repeated with other seeds, so a single run decides it and the seed noise is part of the uncertainty.
  - The behavioural diagnostics (coherence, adjacency, transfer predictability) are recorded, never used as an admission gate; Stage 3 test_recall@10 is the judgement.
  - A proposal that needs an ablation, a sweep or a seed repetition to make its case is out of programme: it has to make the case with one run.
THE SELECTION POLICY (rank-2026-10-v1): the reviewers RANK the proposals. The proposal the reviewers place best, in total, is the round's mechanism. Rank every proposal, best first, and give each one a reason that names the evidence you used.
Read the frozen evidence bundle for each proposal before you place it: a placement you cannot ground in the evidence is not a placement.
Write PLAIN TEXT, one line per proposal, in exactly this shape:
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<1 for the best, then 2, 3, ...> | reason=<one line>
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<n> | reason=<one line>
Every proposal must appear exactly once, the positions must be 1..N with no ties and no gaps, and the reason must say what in the evidence put the proposal there. If you cannot ground a proposal in the evidence, rank it last and say so in its reason; do not leave a proposal out.
THE PROPOSALS:
IDEA: DELTA-PERI-CURV-RQ
TITLE: Per-item Gromov-delta curvature that sets the behaviour-contrastive distance, temperature, weight and quantisation error in one pathway
MOTIVATION: The SID code space is currently organised by text reconstruction, so items that behave alike (co-transition, co-consumption) land far apart and a generative recommender cannot exploit behavioural regularity in the prefix. The probe says the same thing numerically: plain Euclidean RQ-VAE reaches only 0.0402 Spearman against the training behaviour distance and 0.0124 top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap. The fix has to be a training-objective change that makes behavioural proximity a first-class geometric target, not a codebook post-processing.
NOVELTY: The curvature is not set by a schedule, not by prefix-transition scores and not fixed by hand: it is a measured per-item Gromov four-point delta of the behaviour metric, which says how tree-like each item's behavioural neighbourhood is. That single measured number c_i is then used four times at once (distance, temperature, pair weight, commitment error). No dead candidate uses the four-point condition, and none lets a behaviour-derived scalar set the softmax temperature. It is also not a Frechet/Karcher centroid rule, not a radial/cone assignment rule and not a metric swap on frozen code vectors: it changes the Stage-2 objective on the continuous latent that the codes are committed to.
CHANGE: The encoder latent is lifted into a Poincare ball whose curvature is per item, and a behaviour contrastive over training-transition neighbours is computed with that variable-curvature distance, with temperature 1/sqrt(c_ij) and weight c_i*exp(-D_ij/Dbar_i); the same c_i-curved metric replaces the Euclidean RQ commitment error so the code assignment inherits the curvature.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'See SPEC EQUATIONS. In one line: L = L_recon + beta*L_commit + lambda*L_geo, where L_geo is a softmax over batch negatives of the curved distance -d_P^{c_ij}(v_i,v_j)/tau_ij and every ingredient of it (positive set, weight, temperature, curvature) is a function of the training-transition behaviour metric and of its measured Gromov delta. lambda is measured once at initialisation as L_geo(0)/L_recon(0) and frozen; there is no coupling weight to tune.'}
COST: One-off precompute: transition counting over the training sequences, then O(24556 * m^3) quadruple evaluation with m = median positive out-degree (about 20), roughly 2e8 flops, 1-2 min on CPU, and a 24556 x m sparse table of ints/floats (~5 MB). Per step at the frozen scale (batch B = 1024, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs = 72000 steps): one extra B x B = 1.05e6 variable-curvature distance evaluation plus its backward, about 2e7 forward flops and ~6e7 with backward, i.e. roughly +25-40% step time relative to reconstruction-only, and about +35-50 min wall clock on the whole Stage-2 run. Stage 3 is untouched (150 epochs, same protocol). No extra parameters, no extra optimiser state, no second model.
HYPOTHESIS: If behavioural proximity is a tree-like signal, then letting each item's measured tree-likeness set its curvature will align the code space with behaviour much more strongly than any assignment-side change, because the contrastive is computed in exactly the space the probe measures and its negatives are the batch. Observable: Spearman(d_code, d_beh) rises from 0.0402 to at least 0.15 and top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap rises from 0.0124 to at least 0.08; if that holds, the SID prefixes become behaviourally predictable and Stage-3 test_recall@10 should exceed 0.065 (single run, +-0.013 noise).
RISKS: ['(1) The contrastive can overpower reconstruction, producing SIDs that cluster by behaviour but lose item identity, which the generative model then cannot discriminate; lambda balancing at initialisation only protects the start of training. (2) The transition graph is sparse and popularity-skewed, so many items have few or no observed neighbours and get a degenerate delta; the D_max clipping and the m floor are the mitigation but neighbourhood quality is not guaranteed. (3) Variable per-pair curvature is not a true metric (triangle inequality can fail), which is harmless for a softmax but makes "distance" a per-pair functional. (4) If the harness probe computes code-space distance on committed code vectors in plain Euclidean space, the gain depends on the curved commitment making codes track the latent; that link is real but weaker than the latent effect. (5) Extra ~35-50 min of Stage-2 compute may brush against the wall-clock budget.']
END IDEA

IDEA: DELTA-TREE-STRESS-RQ
TITLE: Curvature measured from the behaviour graph's Gromov delta, spent as a curved stress that pulls the quantized RQ code embedding onto the behaviour graph's ultrametric tree, at every prefix depth.
MOTIVATION: The SID code space is organised by text-embedding reconstruction, not by what users actually do, so two items that users swap for each other constantly can sit in unrelated code regions while two near-duplicate descriptions share a long prefix. The probe already shows this: the Euclidean RQ-VAE reaches only 0.0402 Spearman between code-space distance and the training-split behaviour distance, and 0.0124 top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap. The generative recommender then has to spend its prefix budget on a taxonomy that no user behaviour supports, so its beam search over prefixes drifts away from the items the user would actually take next.
NOVELTY: Earlier rounds either changed the metric on frozen codes, or derived curvature from a prefix/transition statistic (per-level prefix-transition score, context entropy, successor profile, behaviour cone). This mechanism derives curvature from a geometric invariant of the behaviour metric itself - the sampled four-point Gromov delta - and it does not use raw graph distance as its target at all: it uses the subdominant ultrametric of the training behaviour metric (MST path-max), which is exactly the kind of metric a negatively curved space represents with low distortion. The curved distance is then applied to the quantized code embedding at every residual prefix depth, weighted by that depth's share of the residual energy, so the coarse SID levels are the ones that must first respect the behaviour tree. No relabelling, no metric swap on fixed codes: the codebook vectors themselves are displaced by a curved stress whose curvature is a measured property of the training behaviour graph.
CHANGE: A single global negative curvature is initialised from the Gromov delta of the training-transition behaviour metric and then learned, and Stage-2 minimises, beside the RQ-VAE loss, a Poincare stress between quantized code embeddings of behaviour-MST-related item pairs whose target is the MST path-max distance; the gradient lands on the codebook entries and on the encoder, so both the codes and the curvature move.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "Offline (CPU, once, training split only): compute n_ij directed training transitions and pop_i; form d_beh(i,j) = -log((n_ij+1)/(sqrt(pop_i*pop_j)+1)); keep the top-K=20 neighbours of each item, symmetrise, take a minimum spanning tree T; store parent pointers and d_T(i,j) = max edge weight on the T path; sample Q=200000 item quadruples to estimate the four-point delta on d_beh, normalise it to delta_tilde and set the initial curvature c_delta = 1/delta_tilde^2. In Stage 2, each step: encode the batch, residual-quantize to get codes k_i^1..k_i^L and the code embedding q_i = sum_l C_l[k_i^l]; for each anchor i sample one near partner j_minus from i's MST children and one far partner j_plus uniformly among items whose normalised tree distance is at least the median; map each prefix embedding into the ball with the curvature-c Poincare exp map; take the Poincare distance at every prefix depth l; regress it on alpha*t_ij with behaviour weights; add lambda times that stress to the RQ-VAE loss. alpha is measured once at the end of epoch 0 and lambda once from the first ten steps' gradient-norm ratio; both are then frozen, as is the curvature's initial value."}
COST: Offline precompute is sub-minute CPU and about 2 MB of sparse-graph state (24556 items x 20 neighbours), no GPU. Per step at the frozen scale the extra work is roughly 2*|batch| anchors (|batch| ~ 1023 at 24556 items / 24 steps) times L=3 prefix depths, i.e. about 6000 Poincare distance evaluations in the encoder width plus one additional backward into the codebook: a low single-digit percentage increase in step time over 72000 steps (3000 epochs x 24). The encoder forward, the text encoder passes and the frozen 150-epoch Stage-3 protocol are untouched, so four-card wall clock grows by a few percent, not a factor.
HYPOTHESIS: If the behaviour metric of the training graph is genuinely tree-like at the scale the SID operates on (delta_tilde well below 0.5) then a curvature set by that delta makes the ultrametric embeddable with small distortion, the curved stress makes code-space distance order items the way training transitions do, and prefix levels inherit that order because they carry most of the residual energy. It is worth keeping if the probe's Spearman rises from 0.0402 to clearly above it (order 0.09-0.15) and top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap rises from 0.0124 toward 0.03 or more, and if that transfer survives into Stage 3 as test_recall@10 above 0.065; a single run carries roughly 0.013 of seed noise, so only a margin larger than that is evidence.
RISKS: ["If delta_tilde is near 0.5 the behaviour metric is not hyperbolic at all and the measured curvature is weak, leaving the stress close to a Euclidean one; the far-pair anchors may be too weak to stop the codebook from contracting; the probe's code-space distance may be a token/prefix distance rather than a distance between code embeddings, in which case the gain arrives only indirectly through prefix alignment; and the frozen alpha and lambda, measured once, could be badly scaled for later epochs."]
END IDEA

IDEA: GDELTA-SUCC-PULL-RQ
TITLE: Behaviour-local Gromov-delta curvature steering a successor-residual pull inside the RQ-VAE code assignment
MOTIVATION: Text-only RQ-VAE SIDs cluster by surface semantics, so items that users actually transition between receive unrelated code prefixes (probe Spearman 0.0402, top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap 0.0124). The recommender therefore has to learn transition structure from SID tokens that were never organised for it. Previous fixes changed the codebook update, a per-level scalar, a radius or a post-hoc score; none changed which code wins at quantization time. This idea changes the assignment decision itself, using the training transition graph and a curved metric, so behaviourally related items are forced into nearby codes during Stage-2.
NOVELTY: (1) the curvature of the quantization metric is an ITEM-level quantity derived from the local Gromov delta of the training transition metric, not a global constant, a per-level value, or an entropy-derived radius; (2) the behaviour signal enters the per-level argmin as a second geodesic term pointing at the curvature-matched centroid of the item's successors' stored residuals, not as a codebook update, a relabelling, or a suffix on an unchanged quantizer; (3) the two distance terms are unit-scaled by detached batch medians, so the coupling weight is derived (=1) and no sweep is needed. No successor-weighted Frechet update, no prefix cone, no successor-profile smoothing, no radial re-ranking, no metric swap on frozen code vectors.
CHANGE: Each residual level assigns the code minimising a two-term curved score d_{K_i}(x_i^l, e_{l,k})/s1 + d_{K_i}(e_{l,k}, g_i^l)/s2 instead of the plain nearest-code distance, where g_i^l is the w_ij-weighted mean of the stored residuals of i's top training successors and K_i is the item curvature from the local Gromov delta of the training transition metric. The chosen indices are the SIDs; the residual recursion, reconstruction and commitment losses are unchanged.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'Precompute once, before Stage-2, from training-split sessions only: n_ij = directed transition counts, pop_i = sum_j n_ij + sum_j n_ji, d_beh(i,j) = -log((n_ij+1)/(sqrt(pop_i*pop_j)+1)); N_i = 4 successors with n_ij>0 and smallest d_beh; w_ij = softmax_j(-d_beh(i,j)) over N_i. Symmetrise l_ij = (d_beh(i,j)+d_beh(j,i))/2; S_i = {i} union N_i union 4 predecessors with largest n_ji (|S_i| <= 9). On the induced subgraph of S_i take shortest-path closure of l (a genuine metric); if disconnected set delta_i = delta_ref. delta_i = max over quadruples (a,b,c,p) in S_i of (largest - second largest)/2 of the three sums d(a,b)+d(c,p), d(a,c)+d(b,p), d(a,p)+d(b,c). delta_ref = median_i delta_i; K_i = clip(delta_ref/(delta_ref+delta_i), 0.1, 2); c0 = 1 is the documented unit-curvature default. During Stage-2, for batch B and level l = 1..L: u_i^1 = Enc(text_i); x_i^l = exp_0(u_i^l) (reference curvature 1), clamp ||x|| <= 0.7; g_i^l = sum_{j in N_i} w_ij * bank[j][l] (stop-grad); s1 = median_i min_k d_{K_i}(x_i^l,e_{l,k}), s2 = median_i min_k d_{K_i}(e_{l,k},g_i^l), both detached and floored at 1e-6; k_i^l = argmin_k [d_{K_i}(x_i^l,e_{l,k})/s1 + d_{K_i}(e_{l,k},g_i^l)/s2]; e_{l,k} = exp_0(v_{l,k}); u_i^{l+1} = log_0(x_i^l) - v_{l,k_i^l}; bank[i][l] <- detach(x_i^l); L = ||Dec(sum_l v_{l,k_i^l}) - text_i||^2 + beta * sum_l ||sg(log_0(x_i^l)) - v_{l,k_i^l}||^2, exactly the baseline losses.'}
COST: 3000 epochs x 24 steps = 72000 steps. Per step the extra work is the second distance term B*K*L = 1023*256*3 ~ 786k Poincare distances (~8 MFLOP) plus two detached medians, roughly 1-3% of a baseline step (encoder/decoder over ~1023 items dominates); no extra backward graph beyond the existing straight-through path. One-off precompute is 24556 items x C(9,4)=126 quadruples (~3.1M small operations, seconds to a minute vectorised) plus one forward pass over 24556 items to fill the residual banks, ~1 epoch-equivalent = 0.03% of the 72000-step budget. Bank memory 24556*3*64*4 B ~ 18.9 MB.
HYPOTHESIS: If transition structure is the missing organising signal, the assignment-level pull must raise the probe above the Euclidean gate, expected Spearman >= 0.10 and top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap >= 0.04 versus 0.0402 / 0.0124, because successors' residuals share codes at every level and therefore share prefixes. Stage-3 test_recall@10 should then exceed 0.065; it is reported as a single run with the explicit ~0.013 noise caveat. If the probe moves but Stage-3 does not, the generative decoder cannot exploit behaviour-organised prefixes, which is itself the informative result.
RISKS: ['The successor pull can concentrate level-1 codes and starve the codebook (monitor per-level usage entropy; the equally unit-scaled text term is the only counterweight). Local delta estimates are noisy for low-degree or disconnected items (fallback delta_ref). Per-item curvature makes the distance a family of Poincare metrics rather than one global manifold. Behaviour smoothing may overwrite fine text distinctions needed for cold or long-tail items, and Stage-3 may lose the SID diversity beam search needs. One run cannot separate these effects from seed noise.']
END IDEA

IDEA: GROMOV-LCA-MOBIUS-RQ
TITLE: Behaviour-tree Gromov products matched by a Möbius-summed curved RQ-VAE code space
MOTIVATION: The frozen semantic-ID pipeline has to place behaviourally adjacent items near each other in code space, yet the plain Euclidean RQ-VAE reaches only Spearman 0.0402 and top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap 0.0124 against the training-split popularity-adjusted transition distance d_beh. The failure is structural: a Euclidean product quantiser cannot represent a tree-like, negatively curved behaviour metric, so co-consumed items fall into unrelated cells even when their text embeddings agree. A behaviour-induced tree, by contrast, embeds in hyperbolic space with arbitrarily low distortion, so the quantiser is given a curved arithmetic and the tree becomes the target the curvature has to realise.
NOVELTY: The earlier rounds moved per-level curvature from prefix entropy (CURVCTRL-SID), ranked items radially by context entropy (BRad-RQ), made codebook updates successor-weighted Fréchet means (poincare-frechet-successor-codebook), and split curvature across branching experts (BRANCHCURV-MOEB-RQ). None of them constructs a behaviour tree, none uses the Gromov product, and none writes the two sides of the objective as the same geometric quantity. This proposal adds two new objects: a spectral bisecting-k-means tree over the popularity-adjusted transition affinity, and an LCA-depth Gromov-product target matched against the Gromov products of Möbius-summed SID points, with the curved residual and geodesic assignment living inside the quantiser rather than being a post-hoc metric or a relabelling of fixed codes.
CHANGE: The RQ residual and the SID point become Möbius operations inside a Poincaré ball (r_l = (−a_l) ⊕ r_{l−1}, x_i = a_1 ⊕ … ⊕ a_L) and every codebook atom is a trainable ball point selected by geodesic distance, so the quantiser is genuinely curved. One extra loss term forces the curved Gromov products of the SID points to reproduce the LCA-depth Gromov products of the behaviour tree, so the same pathway that assigns codes also carries the behaviour gradient into the atoms and the encoder.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'Fix curvature c = 1 and working radius R = 1 − 1e−3. The encoder output z is mapped into the ball, atoms are parametrised inside it, RQ runs by Möbius subtraction, assignment is by geodesic distance, and L = L_recon + L_hier, where L_hier is a relative (ranking) Gromov-product match to a frozen behaviour tree. The tree is built once before Stage 2 from the training-split popularity-adjusted transition affinity: top-50 sparse kNN, rank-64 normalised-spectrum embedding, recursive bisecting 2-means to 64 leaves at depth 6. Every constant is structural or numerical (R from the ball boundary, 64 leaves as a documented default of about 384 items per leaf, beta = 1 because both losses are dimensionless, c = 1) and none is swept.'}
COST: Offline once, before the 3000 epochs: sparse top-50 kNN over 24556 items, a rank-64 randomised SVD of a ~1e6-nnz affinity, six bisecting levels, roughly 3 to 8 minutes on one card, not repeated. Per step at the frozen scale (batch about 1024 of the 24556 training items, 24 steps per epoch, 3000 epochs = 72000 steps): assignments cost L*K*d = 3*256*32 about 25k dot products per sample, about 25 MFLOP per step; three Möbius sums are negligible; the Gromov term evaluates 2*1024 pair distances of dimension 32. Overhead is about 2 to 4 percent of the baseline step, extra memory is one L*K*d atom table, and there is no extra epoch, card or dataloader pass.
HYPOTHESIS: If LCA depth captures the co-consumption hierarchy and the curved code space realises that tree with low distortion, matching Gromov products pulls true successors closer than the Euclidean baseline, visible first as top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap well above 0.0124 (target 0.025 or more) and Spearman well above 0.0402 (target 0.07 or more), then as Stage-3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 under the standing caveat of about 0.013 single-run noise.
RISKS: ['A six-level tree makes the target nearly binary, so the ordering signal may be too coarse; the behaviour gradient may fight text reconstruction and damage the decoder, showing as worse Stage-3 recall even with a better probe; ball saturation could push atoms to the boundary and make geodesic distances uninformative; the tools-side probe may compute code-space distance as Euclidean on stored parameters rather than as a geodesic, so the Euclidean-on-coordinates variant is reported alongside; sparse transitions make n_ij noisy for tail items and can inflate leaf assignment.']
END IDEA

IDEA: SID-GW-DELTA
TITLE: Gromov-delta-calibrated Poincare distance-matrix alignment of the RQ-VAE code space to the training behaviour graph.
MOTIVATION: RQ-VAE Semantic IDs are trained to reconstruct item content, so code-space neighbourhoods reflect content similarity rather than co-consumption. Two items that users actually move between land far apart in code space, and the stage-3 generator has to memorise the transition instead of reading it off the SID prefix. The frozen probe exposes exactly this (Spearman 0.0402, top-10 overlap 0.0124 for the plain Euclidean RQ-VAE).
NOVELTY: The previous mechanisms act per item or per level: behaviour-ranked radial assignment (BRad-RQ), per-level curvature scheduled by a hard prefix-transition score (CURVCTRL-SID), Frechet successor-weighted codebook updates. This one never touches the assignment weights, the codebook update rule or the per-level curvature schedule. It adds a single batch-level term that aligns the entire pairwise distance structure of the code space to the behaviour distance, and it *measures* how hyperbolic the behaviour graph actually is, then fixes the curvature from that measurement instead of scheduling or tuning it.
CHANGE: Stage-2 loss gains one term, L_GW, the discrepancy between normalised pairwise Poincare distances among the batch's decoded code vectors and normalised pairwise behaviour distances among the same items; gradients flow through the straight-through quantizer into both the encoder and the codebooks. The Poincare curvature is a single frozen constant kappa = -1/delta^2, where delta is the estimated 4-point hyperbolicity of a tree built on training transitions.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': '(1) Build the training-only behaviour distance d_beh(i,j) = -log((n_ij+1)/(sqrt(pop_i*pop_j)+1)), symmetrised as min(d_beh(i,j), d_beh(j,i)), from training-split directed transitions only. (2) Build a single-linkage (or neighbour-joining) tree T over the 24556 items from d_beh, estimate delta by sampling 2000 deterministic quadruples and taking max over quadruples of (largest two of the three pairwise sums minus the third)/2; clip delta to [0.01*diam(T), diam(T)]; set kappa = -1/delta^2. (3) At each step, form a batch of 128 anchors, each with its 8 strongest training behaviour neighbours, plus 128 uniform random items: B = 1152. (4) Decode code vectors z_i from the straight-through SID embedding, map to the Poincare ball with exp_0 and clamp radius to 1-1e-5. (5) Compute D_P(i,j) = (2/sqrt|kappa|) artanh(sqrt|kappa| * ||(-z_i) xor z_j||) for pairs present in the batch; compute d_beh for the same pairs from the sparse precomputed table (pairs without an observed transition fall back to their 2-hop shortest path in the transition graph, and are dropped if still absent). (6) Normalise both matrices by their batch medians; L_GW = mean over pairs of (Dhat_P - dhat_beh)^2. Total loss = L_RQVAE + 1.0 * L_GW.'}
COST: One-off CPU precompute of the sparse behaviour kNN and the delta estimate (a few minutes, outside the 3000-epoch budget). Per step only ~9-10k pairs are evaluated, so the extra cost is vectorised Poincare distance plus a sparse lookup: roughly +3-5% wall clock, about +0.3 to +0.6 h over 72k steps (3000 epochs x 24 steps) on four cards. No extra parameters, no extra forward pass.
HYPOTHESIS: If behaviour adjacency is close to tree-like (small delta), a single constant-curvature embedding can realise it with low distortion, and forcing code distances to match it puts transition information into the SID prefixes. Observable as probe Spearman rising above 0.0402 and top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap above 0.0124, with a matching rise in Stage-3 test_recall@10 above 0.065; a single run, so ~0.013 of recall noise is part of the reading.
RISKS: ['The behaviour graph may be far from tree-like, giving a small |kappa| and an almost Euclidean term; the median normalisation can be dominated by the uniform random items and flatten the gradient; sampled neighbour pairs may be too few per batch to move the codebook; the probe may improve while Stage 3 does not, because matching distances is not the same as making prefixes predictive.']
END IDEA

IDEA: LCB-RQ
TITLE: Lorentz co-consumption barycentre targets inside a curved-residual RQ-VAE
MOTIVATION: Behaviourally co-consumed items (same session, close positions) currently get unrelated SIDs because Stage-2 only reconstructs an item's own text embedding; nothing in the objective asks two items that co-occur to share a prefix. The probe numbers of the plain Euclidean RQ-VAE (Spearman 0.0402, top-10 overlap 0.0124) show the code space is behaviour-blind. This proposal moves the quantization target itself along a geodesic toward a behaviour anchor, so co-consumed items are quantized from nearly the same point and must share codes.
NOVELTY: Earlier mechanisms here acted on the codebook update (successor-weighted Frechet means), on per-level curvature from prefix-transition scores, on radial position from context entropy, on cones, on mixed-curvature fibres and on recursive graph cuts. None of them moves the item-side quantization target. LCB-RQ changes what is fed to the quantizer: each item's Lorentzian target is a geodesic barycentre between its own text point and the Lorentz Frechet mean of its co-consumed neighbours' text points, and the whole residual chain then runs in the curved space, so curvature re-shapes level-2 and level-3 residuals rather than only a distance.
CHANGE: Precompute, once from the training split, a symmetric popularity-adjusted co-consumption graph and a per-item Lorentz barycentre of neighbours' text points; during Stage-2 replace each item's quantization point by the geodesic blend of its own text point and that anchor, with the blend weight fixed by measured co-consumption mass, and replace the Euclidean residual recursion by Lorentz exp/log residual quantization with a trainable curvature.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'See SPEC EQUATIONS. In one line: t_i = exp^K_{x_i}( a_i * log^K_{x_i}( b_i ) ), b_i = Frechet_K({x_j : j in N(i)}, pi_ij), a_i = m_i/(m_i + median(m)), and the RQ chain is r_1 = log^K_{c_1}(z), r_{l+1} taken as the log of p_l = exp^K_o(PT(r_l)) at the next code, all distances d_K.'}
COST: Anchor construction is a one-off pass over 24556 items x at most 20 neighbours x 3 fixed-point iterations of exp/log, roughly 1.5M exp/log evaluations, seconds on one GPU, done once before epoch 1 and frozen.
